Explanation: The core value unit is a short e-scooter or e-bike ride that Bird makes available through its app and local fleet network.
Bird runs the rider platform and brand under its current parent, Third Lane Mobility, which acquired Bird's assets in 2024.
Bird has to make reliable vehicles available across many local markets while coordinating riders, operators and cities.
More rides and more well-run local markets increase utilization, revenue and geographic reach.
Bird must manage vehicle quality, operating costs and different local rules across cities.
Bird sells ride access to riders and coordinates fleet work with local operations partners.
Transaction Flows: ← Consumer · Unlock / Pay — Riders unlock a nearby vehicle and pay Bird for the trip. | → Consumer · Ride Access — Bird provides digital access to an available e-scooter or e-bike. | → Provider · Tasks / Tools — Bird sends fleet tasks, routing and support to local operations partners. | ← Provider · Ready Fleet — Operations partners return charged and correctly positioned vehicles to service. | ← Partner · Permit / Space — Cities provide operating permission and define local use of public space. | → Partner · Service / Data — Bird provides micromobility service and operating data for city oversight.

Explanation: Bird sets account, safety and parking rules while adapting the service to each city's requirements.
Bird reaches riders through its app and through city, transit, housing and local partnership programs.
Bird operates the digital platform, supports local operators, manages repairs and coordinates city programs.
Bird contributes the brand, vehicles, app, operational software, routing tools and support systems.
Riders use Bird scooters and e-bikes for short urban trips.
Riders need a quick way to travel short distances without using a car.
A useful vehicle can be found nearby and unlocked directly with the app.
Riders can face limited availability, low battery, poor parking or higher-than-expected trip costs.
Riders unlock a vehicle and pay Bird for the trip.
Transaction Flows: → Owner · Unlock / Pay — Riders unlock a nearby vehicle and pay Bird for the trip. | ← Owner · Ride Access — Bird provides digital access to an available e-scooter or e-bike.

Explanation: The vehicle has to be close enough, charged and allowed in the intended operating zone.
The Bird app shows available vehicles, starts the ride and handles the account and payment flow.
Riders find, unlock, ride and park a vehicle.
Riders contribute an account, payment method, location and trip-demand data.
Local operations partners are businesses that keep Bird fleets charged, positioned and ready for riders.
Operations partners keep vehicles charged and positioned where riders can use them.
Partners earn payouts from completed fleet tasks and can build a local operating business around the Bird network.
Partners need local space, staff, vehicles and time to charge batteries and reposition scooters.
Partners complete Bird-assigned charging, battery-swap and repositioning tasks.
Transaction Flows: ← Owner · Tasks / Tools — Bird sends fleet tasks, routing and support to local operations partners. | → Owner · Ready Fleet — Operations partners return charged and correctly positioned vehicles to service.

Explanation: Bird requires an active compliant business, local insurance and the capacity to support the fleet.
Bird's operations tools provide tasks, routing, guidance and live support.
Partners charge or swap batteries and reposition vehicles; Bird says repairs remain with Bird.
Partners contribute local staff, charging space, vehicles and operational capacity.
Cities authorize and shape Bird programs through permits, rules, street-space decisions and data requirements.
Cities want useful mobility options while keeping streets safe, accessible and orderly.
Shared micromobility can improve first- and last-mile access and support transport or climate goals.
Cities must manage parking, sidewalk obstruction, unsafe riding and uneven service quality.
Cities provide operating permission and rules; Bird provides service and program data.
Transaction Flows: → Owner · Permit / Space — Cities provide operating permission and define local use of public space. | ← Owner · Service / Data — Bird provides micromobility service and operating data for city oversight.

Explanation: Permits, fleet limits, parking rules, speed zones and operating areas differ by city.
Bird works with transport departments and other local public agencies.
Cities issue permits, set operating rules and monitor local program performance.
Cities contribute access to public space, local policy and mobility planning data.
